It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while observing many assemblies that seem to “ape the world’s fads” rather than seeking the “spotless purity of truth,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the purpose of the gathered church and the marks of her legitimacy in this hour? [13, 23, 79, 1441, 1503, 1515, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by “megachurch” spectacles that have replaced the pulpit with a screen, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” that the “gates of hell” will never prevail against the true household of God? [13, 20, 146, 1260, 1408, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with the culture, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs His “vessels for honor” by demanding that we worship Him “in spirit and truth” (John 4:24) [11, 28, 101, 361, 476, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the existence of a church that has lost its way is not an “administrative anomaly” but evidence of a “rebellious heart” that has “exchanged the truth of God for a lie” (Romans 1:25) [15, 68, 1143, 1316, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Great Commission and the Mission of Redemption**

**Verse**
“Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. Amen” (Matthew 28:19–20). [883, 1036, 1617, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “the church has but one mission in this world: to lead people destined to spend eternity in hell to a saving knowledge of Jesus Christ and an eternity in heaven” [40, 75, 161, Conversation History]. The gathered church is to be a “pillar and ground of the truth,” where the “unfailing Word of God” is “rightly preached, explained, applied, and upheld” to “equip the saints for the work of ministry” (1 Timothy 3:15; Ephesians 4:12) [67, 1261, 1284, 1393, 1622, 1642, 1694, Conversation History]. True worship is “not a casual routine” or an “entertainment-hungry” event, but a “spiritual service of worship” where believers “present [their] bodies a living and holy sacrifice” (Romans 12:1) [1, 13, 23, 29, 34, 54, 712, 1101, 1444, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “market-driven strategy” that treats the gospel like a “commodity to be sold,” for “your life is not your own” and neither is the mission of the church (1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [12, 91, 101, 298, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1597, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “the Word of God is not chained” by human methodology, and your “sole objective” is to find “repose of the soul” in Christ’s “finished work” while “shining as lights in the world” (2 Timothy 2:9; John 19:30; Philippians 2:15) [24, 25, 41, 101, 123, 142, 906, 907, 1268, 1283, 1406, 1420, 1445, 1504, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious aristocracy” was often “punctilious” about “legal minutiae,” yet they “neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith” (Matthew 23:23) [8, 152, 176, 177, 1091, 1094, 1352, 1461, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the concept of the sanctuary, revealing that “the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands,” for “the church militant” is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” whose “true home” is the “heavenly Jerusalem” (Acts 7:48; Hebrews 12:22) [5, 11, 13, 26, 38, 142, 612, 1021, 1042, 1255, 1281, 1313, 1316, 1320, 1426, 1646, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Preeminence of the Only True Head**

**Verse**
“And He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things He may have the preeminence” (Colossians 1:18). [293, 414, 855, 856, 1199, 1315, 1322, 1528, 1627, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture claims that “Jesus Christ alone is the head of the church,” and any attempt by a “politician,” “popue,” or “pastor” to “usurp the title” is a “spirit of fraud” [291, 412, 415, 1233, 1528, 1627, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. A true church is one that “holds fast to the Head,” recognizing that “the Father has given Him authority over us” and his rule is “mediated... solely and only by His revealed truth” (Colossians 2:19; Ephesians 1:22) [26, 30, 31, 293, 1132, 1144, 1406, 1528, 1622, 1625, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. Assemblies that “minimizing both the Word of God and the lordship of Christ” to “gain mass appeal” are not building the true church but “religious empires” designed for “self-satisfaction” [20, 288, 298, 1595, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” and “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [5, 11, 13, 21, 24, 31, 43, 64, 103, 136, 1132, 1143, 1199, 1315, 1408, 1515, 1572, 1616, 1720, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” refusing to follow “blind guides” who “pander for publicity” rather than “ascribing greatness to our God” (Deuteronomy 32:3; Matthew 15:14) [11, 79, 116, 444, 1072, 1131, 1179, 1313, 1406, 1411, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of Authority**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, God “removed kings from their thrones” when they “rejected the word of the LORD” (1 Samuel 15:23) [7, 15, 17, 1078, 1183, 1533, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” showing that we must “refuse to yield submission” to any authority that tries to “tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel,” for “we ought to obey God rather than men” (Acts 5:29; Galatians 2:5) [19, 1130, 1144, 1176, 1217, 1247, 1256, 1300, 1316, 1370, 1431, 1529, 1638, 1720, Conversation History].

### **Section 3: The Fruit of Truth vs. Whitewashed Tombs**

**Verse**
“ ‘Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs which indeed appear beautiful outwardly, but inside are full of dead men’s bones and all uncleanness. Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness’ ” (Matthew 23:27–28). [122, 188, 189, 1347, 1472, 1486, 1543, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer** and **Voddie Baucham**—teaches that “each tree is known by its own fruit,” and a true church is distinguished by “spiritual fruit” and “sanctification” rather than “flashy showmanship” (Luke 6:44) [6, 13, 146, 253, 254, 307, 367, 369, 437, 712, 715, 803, 1406, Conversation History]. Assemblies that possess a “patchwork faith” or “stitch together a variety of religious ideas” often have a “form of godliness but deny its power” (2 Timothy 3:5) [161, 1655, Conversation History]. Those who “practice lawlessness” (*anomia*) by living “as though He never gave a law to obey” prove that they “never truly believed in the first place” (1 John 2:19) [165, 260, 1396, 1505, 1508, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “perfect justice will come” and He will “judge between the nations,” exposing the “spirit of fraud” in every “idolatrous” assembly (Isaiah 2:4; 1 Thessalonians 1:10) [11, 14, 24, 37, 94, 109, 152, 174, 201, 210, 412, 470, 719, 816, 822, 948, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by resting upon the “surest foundation,” for if you “abide in My word,” the “Spirit of truth” will “guide you into all truth” (John 8:31; 16:13) [11, 13, 24, 47, 92, 113, 121, 125, 133, 142, 164, 176, 201, 332, 352, 412, 602, 630, 813, 855, 856, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1336, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1494, 1503, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: From Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” were “shadows” that could not “eliminate sin,” but pointed toward the Savior [11, 13, 32, 142, 394, 911, 1313, 1344, 1345, 1430, 1440, 1442, 1443, 1482, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our vision of “sacred space,” revealing that “your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit,” and we find “repose of the soul” not in “ritualized ceremonies” but in “the renewing of your mind” (1 Corinthians 6:19; Romans 12:2) [11, 12, 13, 17, 24, 101, 136, 142, 157, 186, 238, 240, 264, 446, 464, 469, 476, 612, 630, 790, 833, 860, 899, 1042, 1059, 1093, 1119, 1128, 1129, 1138, 1202, 1243, 1262, 1267, 1313, 1316, 1406, 1417, 1426, 1445, 1529, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

### **Section 4: Contending for the Biblical Foundation**

**Verse**
“Beloved, while I was very diligent to write to you concerning our common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints” (Jude 3). [750, 760, 1137, 1141, 1246, 1334, 1358, 1389, 1440, 1461, 1463, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Martin Luther**—asserts that “it is actually a sin not to fight when vital truths are under attack,” for the church is called to defend the “spotless purity of truth” against “savage wolves” [1325, 1354, 1441, 1461, 1500, 1601, 1638, Conversation History]. An assembly that has “lost its biblical foundation” is often one that has replaced “biblical preaching” with “drama teams,” “film crews,” or “empty platitudes” [146, 313, 348, 1197, 1634, Conversation History]. “Apostasy” is defined as “hearing the truth, knowing what it is, professing to accept it, and then finally rejecting it,” and it frequently “creeps in unnoticed” through leaders who “love the world” (1 John 2:15) [12, 185, 326, 356, 397, 398, 400, 402, 547, 548, 549, 550, 582, 583, 893, 1502, 1527, 1536, 1537, 1543, 1547, 1605, 1624, 1631, 1636, 1641, 1651, 1666, 1687, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “opinion polls” or “subjective feelings,” for “the Bible is the source of truth” and is “totally sufficient for your needs” (2 Timothy 3:16–17; Psalm 119:105) [51, 101, 123, 145, 163, 209, 456, 526, 598, 657, 859, 861, 878, 879, 1062, 1312, 1313, 1331, 1333, 1334, 1381, 1398, 1406, 1411, 1414, 1448, 1453, 1461, 1503, 1515, 1532, 1684, 1709, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “examine everything carefully” to ensure your assembly is “built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ Himself being the chief cornerstone” (Proverbs 28:26; Ephesians 2:20) [11, 13, 87, 90, 101, 116, 123, 132, 172, 181, 209, 212, 251, 294, 295, 396, 403, 404, 433, 523, 526, 534, 538, 539, 542, 584, 586, 591, 654, 673, 842, 844, 855, 856, 858, 861, 914, 1017, 1039, 1051, 1072, 1073, 1081, 1083, 1098, 1101, 1109, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1144, 1217, 1223, 1230, 1233, 1235, 1242, 1243, 1256, 1261, 1262, 1284, 1300, 1306, 1313, 1315, 1316, 1317, 1321, 1322, 1324, 1325, 1329, 1332, 1333, 1340, 1341, 1343, 1344, 1346, 1349, 1351, 1354, 1358, 1361, 1364, 1365, 1371, 1373, 1374, 1381, 1383, 1387, 1389, 1391, 1393, 1395, 1396, 1397, 1398, 1399, 1401, 1406, 1407, 1408, 1411, 1420, 1421, 1423, 1424, 1431, 1445, 1448, 1450, 1451, 1453, 1458, 1461, 1463, 1465, 1466, 1467, 1468, 1470, 1473, 1474, 1479, 1480, 1484, 1487, 1490, 1493, 1494, 1495, 1497, 1500, 1501, 1502, 1503, 1512, 1513, 1515, 1520, 1524, 1528, 1529, 1532, 1542, 1545, 1563, 1567, 1572, 1573, 1581, 1583, 1594, 1597, 1601, 1605, 1611, 1613, 1614, 1616, 1617, 1622, 1634, 1636, 1638, 1642, 1646, 1649, 1653, 1662, 1664, 1665, 1666, 1667, 1670, 1672, 1675, 1680, 1684, 1692, 1694, 1702, 1709, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 291, 300, 304, 311, 313, 319, 324, 325, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 424, 444, 449, 591, 834, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: The Pharisees, through their rabbinic tradition, had succeeded in corrupting and perverting all the good things God had taught the nation of Israel, including their practice of prayer. No religion has ever had a higher standard and priority for prayer than Judaism. As God’s chosen people, the Jews were the recipients of His written Word, “entrusted with the oracles of God” (Rom. 3:2). No other people as a race or as a nation has ever been so favored by God or had such direct communication with Him.

That is why Paul referred to the atonement as “the testimony given [by Christ] at the proper time.” This thought precisely parallels Galatians 4:4–5: “But when the fullness of the time came, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the Law, so that He might redeem those who were under the Law.” Christ “gave Himself as a ransom” at exactly “the proper time” in God’s redemptive plan. His redemptive work is the most eloquent testimony ever borne to God’s saving desire for sinners. Evangelistic prayer for all men therefore reflects the heart of God and honors Christ’s work on the cross.

Furthermore, there is a clear and significant difference between a parable (a story made up by Jesus to illustrate a precept, proposition, or principle) and history (a chronicle of events that actually happened). The parable helps explain a truth; history gives a factual account of what happened. Although history is told in story form, it is not illustrative fiction but reality. One of the main ways the essential propositions of Christian truth have been preserved and passed down to us is by including them in the infallible record of biblical history. Again, that is the very principle on which Paul built his argument about the truth of bodily resurrection in 1 Corinthians 15.

Authentic faith is a “saving grace whereby we receive [Jesus Christ] and rest upon him alone for salvation as he is offered to us in the gospel.” Those words are borrowed from the Westminster Shorter Catechism (question 86). The larger catechism (question 72) says, Justifying faith is a saving grace, wrought in the heart of a sinner by the Spirit and Word of God, whereby he, being convinced of his sin and misery, and of the disability in himself and all other creatures to recover him out of his lost condition, not only assents to the truth of the promise of the gospel, but receives and rests upon Christ and his righteousness, therein held forth, for pardon of sin, and for the accepting and accounting of his person righteous in the sight of God for salvation.

That is the failure referred to in Luke 16:9. The proper translation is not “when you fail” (nkjv), but “when it fails”: “Make friends for yourselves by unrighteous mammon, that when it [the mammon fails], they [the friends] may receive you into an everlasting home.” The clear implication is that it is every believer’s duty to invest the temporary value of unrighteous mammon in an enterprise that will reap far greater, eternal value—by putting our money to work for ministry to the people of God, and especially for the spread of gospel truth. The relationships gained through such investments will enrich heaven for eternity. Nothing else we do with our money will last forever.

When Jesus reached the end of the parable of the unjust steward in Luke 16, some Pharisees overheard Him warning His disciples against making an idol of money: “You cannot serve God and mammon” (Luke 16:13). Luke says, “Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they derided Him” (v. 14). Jesus replied with yet another forceful condemnation of their religion. He pointed out that although the Pharisees labored nonstop to make it look as though they were serious, diligent, and single-minded in their devotion to the law, the reality was that their religion was too superficial. God was not impressed. Their best-looking good works were of no more value in the eyes of God than a pile of nasty rags soiled and stained with bodily fluids. I realize that imagery is revolting in the extreme, but it faithfully conveys the literal meaning of Isaiah 64:6. It reflects God’s utter contempt for self-righteousness and human religion. Jesus told them: “You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is highly esteemed among men is an abomination in the sight of God” (Luke 16:15, emphasis added).

Thus, to be a Christian, in the true sense of the term, is to be a wholehearted follower of Jesus Christ. As the Lord Himself said in John 10:27, “My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me” (emphasis added). The name suggests much more than a superficial association with Christ. Rather, it demands a deep affection for Him, allegiance to Him, and submission to His Word. “You are My friends if you do what I command you,” Jesus told His disciples in the Upper Room (John 15:14). Earlier He told the crowds who flocked to hear Him, “If you continue in My word, then you are truly disciples of Mine” (John 8:31); and elsewhere: “If anyone wishes to come after Me, he must deny himself, and take up his cross daily and follow Me” (Luke 9:23; cf. John 12:26).

In a sermon entitled “Jesus Our Lord,” Spurgeon made the issue crystal clear: The Church of God, in a very special manner, calls Jesus “our Lord,” for there is not, and there cannot be any head of the Church except the Lord Jesus Christ. It is awful blasphemy for any man on earth to call himself Christ’s vicar and the head of the church, and it is a usurpation of the crown rights of King Jesus for any king or queen to be called the head of the church, for the true Church of Jesus Christ can have no head but Jesus Christ himself. I am thankful that there is no head to the church of which I am a member save Jesus Christ himself, nor dare I be a member of any church which would consent to any headship but his.28

In Roman times, it was not uncommon for dozens, or even hundreds, of slaves to serve the same master.13 As members of his extended household, they were accountable to the one master both as a group and as individuals. The same is true of the church, where Christ is the head not merely of the corporate body but also of each individual believer. He is both the Savior and the Lord for each person who calls on Him (Acts 2:21). When we call Jesus “Lord,” we are clearly acknowledging Him as sole Master. The Greek word for “Lord” is kyrios, and it occurs nearly 750 times in the New Testament. Its fundamental meaning is “master,” or “owner,” making it the relational counterpart to the word slave (doulos).14 As Murray Harris explains:

As Paul explained to Timothy: The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness.” Now in a large house there are not only gold and silver vessels, but also vessels of wood and of earthenware, and some to honor and some to dishonor. Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work. Now flee from youthful lusts and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. (2 Tim. 2:19–22)
